accuracy.reference: PyTorch model runtime following checkpoint and input_spec dtypes
accuracy.target: SWFT DSL model input/output dtypes matching golden model input/output dtypes

stages.name: Torch IR export and validation
stages.objective: Build a deterministic exporter around the trusted PyTorch model. Use model_config.json to locate the target class, constructor kwargs, and entry method. Infer and export input_spec.json from the model code and weights, then export a machine-readable IR, node manifest, weight map, and torch runner. Validate the exported artifacts against the original PyTorch model before downstream stages consume them.
procedure: Read model_config.json first. Treat model_class, model_kwargs, and entry_method as the authoritative model entry configuration. Treat the INPUT_MANIFEST torch_weights path as the authoritative weight file.
Load the torch_model_source and torch_weights paths from INPUT_MANIFEST.json, instantiate the configured class with model_kwargs, switch to eval mode, and disable gradients.
Infer model entry inputs and write input_spec.json with names, shapes, dtypes, construction method, and reproducibility seed.
Export model_ir.json, node_manifest.json, and weight_map.json from the trusted PyTorch execution path.
Write torch_runner.py so downstream stages can run the model and capture intermediates without rereading the full torch_model_source file.
Run validation that compares the exported runner and IR assumptions against the original PyTorch model, then write export_validation_report.json.
quality_checks: Do not ask the user for input_spec.json; this stage owns generating it.
Do not hard-code a class name from the model source if model_config.json provides one.
Record every checkpoint tensor's dtype and shape in weight_map.json; do not silently cast weights to fp32.
input_spec.json must explicitly define model entry input dtype, shape, seed, and construction method.
The exported runner must be deterministic and usable by later stages.
judge_checklist: model_config.json fields were actually used to instantiate and call the model.
input_spec.json is derived from the model entry and contains enough information to recreate inputs.
weight_map.json records checkpoint dtype and shape for every weight tensor.
torch_runner.py can load weights and invoke the configured entry_method.
model_ir.json, node_manifest.json, and weight_map.json are consistent with export_validation_report.json.

stages.name: IR partition plan
stages.objective: Split the validated machine-generated Torch IR into SWFT-friendly partitions. Do not reinterpret the original PyTorch source unless the IR validation report explicitly marks an ambiguity.
procedure: Read the validated IR, node manifest, weight map, and export validation report.
Read the similar DSL only for implementation patterns and likely fusion boundaries, not as a semantic source for the target model.
Create partitions that cover the full IR with explicit inputs, outputs, dependencies, node ids, dtypes, and shapes.
For every partition, write semantic_deps, implementation_deps, fusion_group, can_implement_independently, input_contract, and output_contract.
Mark fusion opportunities, cube/matmul regions, expected tiling axes, and SWFT implementation risks such as concat plus non-regular nd_to_nz.
Write partition_plan.json for machines and partition_plan.md for humans.
quality_checks: Every IR node is assigned to exactly one partition unless explicitly documented as metadata or no-op.
Partition boundaries expose all cross-partition tensors.
The plan considers SWFT alignment and fusion constraints before DSL implementation starts.
judge_checklist: The partition plan covers the complete validated IR without duplicate ownership.
Each partition has clear inputs, outputs, node list, shape/dtype metadata, and dependencies.
Each partition declares semantic_deps and implementation_deps so stage 05 can decide which subagents can run in parallel.
The plan uses SWFT implementation notes to flag risky concat, transpose, matmul, and padding areas.
The plan does not depend on rereading full PyTorch source for normal downstream work.

stages.name: Torch per-partition golden generation
stages.objective: Use the validated torch runner, inferred input_spec, and partition plan to capture deterministic per-partition input and output bins directly from the trusted PyTorch model, following checkpoint and input_spec dtypes.
procedure: Use torch_runner.py and input_spec.json to construct deterministic model inputs with exactly the dtypes recorded in input_spec.json.
Run the trusted PyTorch model following the checkpoint tensor dtypes and input_spec dtypes; do not force fp32 unless those artifacts require fp32.
Write binary files under output/cases with stable names and record all paths in golden_manifest.json.
Record dtype, shape, byte order, partition id, source node ids, random seed, and whether the tensor is model IO or partition intermediate for every bin.
Write torch_golden_report.json with reproducibility and sanity-check details.
quality_checks: Golden outputs must come from PyTorch model runtime, not NumPy and not DSL.
Model-level DSL inputs and outputs must use the same dtype as the model-level golden inputs and outputs.
Manifest paths must exist and point to non-empty files.
Every partition in partition_plan.json must have corresponding golden inputs and outputs.
judge_checklist: golden_manifest.json covers all partitions and full-model outputs.
All recorded bins exist, are non-empty, and have dtype/shape metadata.
torch_golden_report.json shows the runner followed checkpoint dtypes and input_spec dtypes.
The manifest makes model IO dtypes explicit so DSL execution can match them.
No golden is generated from DSL or from a hand-written NumPy reference.

stages.name: SWFT DSL skeleton
stages.objective: Create a minimal SWFT DSL harness that proves compile, run, file input, and file output work before real partition implementation starts. The skeleton should exercise GM->UB->GM for the first suitable tensor.
procedure: Read SWFT_DSL_FLOW and SWFT_IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES before writing DSL.
Pick the first suitable tensor from golden_manifest.json and build a minimal GM input -> UB -> GM output path.
Use slice_to_ub for reading and insert_to_gm for writing unless a documented reason requires otherwise.
Call compile_kernel and exec_kernel, confirm .cce, generated main.cpp, actual output bin, and comparison result.
Write target_model_dsl.py and skeleton_run_report.json with commands, paths, device id, and pass/fail details.
quality_checks: This stage should not implement real model math beyond the IO skeleton.
The skeleton must prove file input, file output, compile, and execution all work.
The report must state where .cce, generated main.cpp, input bin, golden bin, and actual bin were produced.
judge_checklist: target_model_dsl.py contains a real compile_kernel and exec_kernel path.
The skeleton performs GM -> UB -> GM and uses explicit file inputs/outputs.
skeleton_run_report.json contains actual command evidence and comparison result.
No real partition implementation is hidden in the skeleton stage.

stages.name: SWFT DSL partition implementations
stages.objective: The main agent coordinates multiple subagents. Each subagent implements one or more disjoint partitions using the partition plan and torch-generated golden bins. The main agent integrates accepted partition implementations.
procedure: Generate partition subagent packages with package_dsl_subagents.py.
Read subagent_task_manifest.json to distinguish ready_partitions and blocked_partitions.
For manual launch, open one fresh agent session per ready partition package and give it only that package path.
Do not launch blocked partitions until implementation_deps are resolved or the main agent groups them with their dependency/fusion group.
Require every subagent to compile, run, and compare its partition against torch-generated golden with the configured partition tolerance.
Subgraph tests should feed each DSL partition with torch-captured partition inputs so partition errors are isolated.
Review subagent outputs and integrate only partitions with passing correctness reports.
Write partition_impl_manifest.json, dsl_progress.json, partition_correctness_report.json, and validation_notes.md.
quality_checks: Subagents must not edit each other's partition outputs.
Subagents must write only their partition-owned implementation.py, correctness_report.json, validation_notes.md, and artifacts.
Every implemented partition must have a correctness report with relative error or a documented override.
The main agent must clearly list accepted, rejected, blocked, and missing partitions.
judge_checklist: subagent_task_manifest.json matches the partition plan.
subagent_task_manifest.json clearly separates ready_partitions and blocked_partitions.
partition_impl_manifest.json includes only partitions with evidence-backed correctness reports.
partition_correctness_report.json compares DSL actuals against torch-generated golden bins with the configured partition tolerance, or records a documented override.
dsl_progress.json clearly reports implemented and pending partitions.

stages.name: Full DSL integration and correctness
stages.objective: Integrate all accepted partition implementations into a single full-model SWFT DSL program and validate final correctness against torch-generated full-model outputs with matching model IO dtypes.
procedure: Integrate accepted partition implementations into one target_model_dsl.py.
Preserve the skeleton's compile and exec_kernel flow.
Run the full graph DSL using model-level input/output dtypes that match golden_manifest.json.
Write full_correctness_report.json with relative error, max error, compared files, and command evidence.
Do not begin performance-only rewrites in this stage.
quality_checks: Every partition in the plan must be covered or explicitly reported as unsupported.
Full-model correctness must be checked against torch-generated full-model output.
The integrated DSL must be the artifact that 07_perf will optimize.
judge_checklist: target_model_dsl.py covers all accepted partitions and preserves the SWFT execution chain.
full_correctness_report.json proves full-model DSL output vs torch-generated full-model output passed the final tolerance.
No partition is silently skipped.
The output is ready for formal interface packaging in 07_perf.

stages.name: Latency optimization
stages.objective: Optimize the already-correct DSL until latency is within target while preserving the required final accuracy bound. Final latency must be measured through the formal interface path, not only through Python exec_kernel profiling.
procedure: Read SWFT_PERF_GUIDE and SWFT_INTERFACE_FLOW before changing DSL.
Create a formal interface package from the correctness-passing DSL, generated .cce, input bins, golden bins, and host entry.
Measure baseline latency through the formal interface path.
Optimize tiling, fusion, core partitioning, memory layout, and GM traffic while preserving correctness.
After every meaningful optimization, rerun correctness against torch-generated full-model golden.
Write final target_model_dsl.py, interface_package, formal_run_report.json, perf_report.json, optimization_log.md, full_correctness_report.json, and validation_notes.md.
quality_checks: Final reported latency must come from the formal interface path.
Correctness must remain within the configured tolerance after optimization.
The optimization log must explain each change and its measured impact.
If 200us is not reached, the report must identify the likely bottleneck and attempted optimizations.
judge_checklist: formal_run_report.json proves non-Python interface execution was used.
perf_report.json includes baseline latency, final latency, measurement method, and whether latency_target_us was met.
full_correctness_report.json still passes after the final optimization.
optimization_log.md is specific enough to reproduce the tuning path.
